INVALID: is_error true, terminal_reason api_error, api_error_status 429, result text reports an individual spend limit hit, session limit resets 4:50pm (Europe/Berlin). Died at 4 turns, cost 0.18 list-price before failing. Per the protocol delta's If-blocked clause: marked invalid, not replaced; the package paused (parked needs-human) and resumed after the reset time passed (confirmed independently against the developer's own system clock, which read past the reset time on resume). One permission_denial is a compound Bash command that does not match a single allowlisted pattern, expected allowlist behavior, unrelated to the 429.

INVALID: contamination gate hit. One Glob tool_use, {pattern: **/issues-open.json, path: /Users/TM/.cache/orchestrai-lead-trial} (the parent of both trial roots, not this run's own repo), whose tool_result returned a file path under the 2026-09-23 sibling root. All other tool inputs in this run stayed inside the 2026-09-28 root. Otherwise a clean completion: not budget-capped, no other gate failure, no em dashes found in the final message. This is the same class of filesystem-jail gap #358 documented (Glob/Grep/Read are not confined to the cloned repo), landing this time on the sibling trial root itself rather than an installed skills directory.

INVALID: contamination gate hit, same class as H2. One Glob tool_use, {pattern: **/_snapshot*, path: /Users/TM/.cache/orchestrai-lead-trial} (the parent of both trial roots). Its own result was 'No files found' (the pattern does not match a bare directory name), so unlike H2 this call leaked no content from the 2026-09-23 root; applying the gate's literal text (any tool input whose path argument scopes in the 2026-09-23 root) rather than an effect-based reading, for consistency with H2 and to avoid a post-hoc call that happens to favor this run. This is a repeatable structural gap, not a fluke: Glob is granted by --allowedTools with no path restriction (unlike the Bash(...) patterns, which do restrict by command form), so any run that Globs from an unscoped absolute path can sweep the sibling root; worth flagging for any future trial using this same allowlist. Separately, and not a gate violation under this protocol delta's forbidden-path list (~/.hermes is not on it): one Glob and one Read touched /Users/TM/.hermes/skills/autonomous-ai-agents/orchestrai/, the same filesystem-jail class #358 already documented (F1, O1, F2). Otherwise a clean completion: not budget-capped, no other gate failure, no em dashes found.

Valid. Round 2, new trial root with no 2026-09-23 sibling. Clean completion, not budget-capped, effort gate passes (all perTurnEffort high), contamination gate clear (the one Glob call outside the repo was scoped to this run's own 2026-09-28-r2 root, which has no 2026-09-23 sibling to sweep in), no ~/.hermes reads this run, no em dashes or banned phrases in the final message.

no_writes_check_h4_h6.note: added in the PR #408 fix round (reviewer finding 3); the original no_writes_check block above used a window starting at H1's start and named only H1-H3, so H4-H6 had no recorded check of their own. Run read-only, after the fact, about 2 days after H4-H6 finished.
no_writes_check_h4_h6.verdict: no result traces to a write by H4, H5, or H6 (same GH_CONFIG_DIR-empty, Bash(gh *)-disallowed setup as H1-H3; none of the three raw run logs contains a gh or git-push tool call), but this check ran about 2 days after H4-H6 finished, so the window also catches every issue/PR touched by all later, unrelated repo work (subsequent batches and fix rounds) in between; it no longer isolates H4-H6's own writes as tightly as the same-day H1-H3 check did.
